title: STRANGE MINUTE #21
endSub: What should it say about us?

lines.text: This tiny probe is now one light-day from Earth.
Voyager 1 left Earth in 1977. Before smartphones. Before the internet.
lines.say: Voyager 1 left Earth in nineteen seventy-seven. Before smartphones. Before the internet.

lines.text: It's been flying ever since, at about 38,000 miles per hour.
lines.say: It's been flying ever since, at about thirty-eight thousand miles per hour.

lines.text: Now it's so far that light needs a whole day to reach it.
That's about 16 billion miles. Nothing we've built has ever gone farther.
lines.say: That's about sixteen billion miles. Nothing we've built has ever gone farther.

lines.text: Drive there at highway speed? About 28,000 years.
lines.say: Drive there at highway speed? About twenty-eight thousand years.

lines.text: Its radio is about as strong as a fridge light bulb.
And giant dishes on Earth still catch that whisper.
Its nuclear battery is slowly fading.
So NASA keeps switching instruments off, one by one, to save power.
On board: a golden record with music and greetings from Earth.
Long after it goes silent, it will keep drifting between the stars.
So if someone out there finds it... what should it say about us?

sources: NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 approaching one light-day (~16.1 billion mi / 25.9 billion km) in Nov 2026; launched Sept 5, 1977; ~38,000 mph (17 km/s)
